content.title: Read and Change the Page
content.hook: Finding an element is only half the job. Next, read or change what is inside it.
content.context: Finding an element is only half the job. Next, read or change what is inside it.
goals: Read visible text from an element and change visible text deliberately with `textContent`.

content.title: Reading text
content.text:
Given: ```html

Waiting

``` You can read its current text: ```js const status = document.querySelector("#status"); console.log(status.textContent); ``` The result is the string `Waiting`.

content.title: Changing text
content.text:
You can assign a new value:

```js
status.textContent = "Ready";
```

The browser updates the current page so the paragraph displays `Ready`.

content.question:
What appears on the page after this code runs? ```html

Waiting

```

activities.title: Change one thing
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt:
Start with: ```html

Good morning

``` Write JavaScript that changes the heading to `Good afternoon`. ```js const message = document.querySelector("#message"); message.textContent = "Good afternoon"; ```
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.

feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.title: One important distinction
content.text:
Changing `textContent` changes the text inside the current element. It does not change which element you selected.

That gives you a useful two-step pattern:

**Select → Change**

```js
const message = document.querySelector("#message");
message.textContent = "Good afternoon";
```

content.question:
A learner says, "I changed the paragraph, so I changed the HTML file."

What is the better explanation?

options.text: The browser changed the live page structure; the original file on disk was not rewritten by `textContent`.
JavaScript always edits files on the computer.
The browser sent the paragraph to a server.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. The browser changed the live page structure; the original file on disk was not rewritten by `textContent`.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. The browser changed the live page structure; the original file on disk was not rewritten by `textContent`.
